title: Anti CEC Protest Live Updates: Cops at Dipke's home, serve notice barring him from holding Tiranga march
summary: The Delhi Police served notice to CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke barring him from holding Tiranga march on Friday at 5pm at CP park.
body:
The Delhi Police served notice to CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke barring him from holding Tiranga march on Friday at 5pm at CP park.

Delhi is on high alert as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, prepares for its proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march in Connaught Place. Delhi Police has deployed around 6,000 personnel, backed by 200 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) in shifts, as authorities step up security across central Delhi amid uncertainty over the gathering.

The march is scheduled for 5pm on October 16 at Central Park, Connaught Place. The CJP has appealed to citizens to join the gathering with the national flag, pitching the campaign as a fight to protect voting rights and the right to protest. However, the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) has announced that Central Park will remain closed on Friday. Police have also indicated that Jantar Mantar is no longer a designated protest site, with demonstrations permitted at alternative venues subject to approval.

The proposed march comes amid the CJP’s ongoing campaign against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The party has alleged large-scale voter deletions and called for accountability. The dispute has intensified following the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were sent to five days of judicial custody after entering Jantar Mantar and raising slogans demanding the CEC’s resignation.

Security arrangements include barricades, body-worn cameras and restrictions on movement at key locations. The Delhi Traffic Police has warned that traffic on 21 roads and stretches in central Delhi could be affected from 3pm, with diversions depending on the situation.

title: Virginia has acquired 2,211 acres around Buffalo Mountain to create a new conservation area, protecting nearly 14 miles of native trout streams and expanding a landscape already drawing 15,000 visitors a year
summary: There are landscapes that become part of a place’s identity long before they receive an official designation.
body:
Buffalo Mountain’s new conservation area offers scenic landscapes, protected forests and outdoor experiences near the Blue Ridge Parkway and Blacksburg.

There are landscapes that become part of a place’s identity long before they receive an official designation. Buffalo Mountain, with its rounded summit, expansive views and deep Appalachian forests, has long been one of Southwest Virginia’s most recognisable natural landmarks. Now, more than 2,200 additional acres around the mountain are set to remain protected, giving the landscape a stronger shield against future development, states an online release by the official website of the Commonwealth of Virginia.

A major expansion of protected land

According to the release, Virginia has established a new State Conservation Area at Buffalo Mountain following the acquisition of 2,211 acres across Floyd and Carroll counties. The property surrounds the existing Buffalo Mountain Natural Area Preserve, creating a larger protected landscape and bringing the total acreage of Department of Conservation and Recreation-owned land at Buffalo Mountain to 4,332 acres, adds the online report.If we go by the release, the acquisition was carried out in partnership with The Conservation Fund, with $9.5 million in federal Forest Legacy Program funding helping make the purchase possible.

The newly protected property will be managed by the Department of Conservation and Recreation, which plans to develop a management strategy and expand opportunities for public access. The move builds on decades of conservation efforts in the area. An earlier phase of the project added 975 acres to the existing natural area preserve, taking the dedicated preserve to 2,121 acres, claims the online release.

Protecting forests and trout streams

The importance of the acquisition extends well beyond hiking trails and scenic overlooks. The property contains nearly 14 miles of native trout streams, including waterways supporting wild populations of eastern brook trout and brown trout. These streams sit within the headwaters of the New River, an important water source for communities in Virginia and West Virginia. The river provides drinking water to more than 675,000 people, making the protection of surrounding forests and waterways an important part of maintaining water quality. The landscape is also home to extensive mature forests, including Southern Appalachian Rich Cove Forest, a habitat type known for its ecological diversity. Keeping the surrounding acreage intact creates a buffer for the existing natural area preserve while helping protect wildlife habitat and forest connectivity.

A destination for outdoor enthusiasts

Located in a rural part of Southwest Virginia, the conservation area lies only a few miles from the Blue Ridge Parkway and less than 50 miles from the growing Blacksburg area. Buffalo Mountain has already established itself as a popular destination, with about 15,000 people visiting the preserve each year, claims the online report. The summit is a major draw, offering broad views across the surrounding Appalachian landscape. With the new conservation area, visitors will eventually have access to more opportunities for low-impact recreation while the most sensitive natural resources remain protected.

Conservation with a long-term view

The project also represents a significant collaboration between state and federal conservation agencies, The Conservation Fund and the Lawson family, which had owned the property for more than a century. The land was acquired by The Conservation Fund before being transferred to Virginia for permanent protection, adds the report. Federal Forest Legacy funding for the purchase comes through the Land and Water Conservation Fund, which supports conservation and recreation projects across the country. With the Buffalo Mountain acquisition, a landscape shaped by generations of private stewardship is now entering a new chapter as public land. Images Courtesy: istock

title: Tesla's 'flying car' Roadster stuns in demo: How high can it fly and what will it cost?
summary: Tesla unveils its next-gen Roadster with rocket thrusters, mid-air manoeuvres and a dramatic landing demonstration.
body:
Tesla unveils its next-gen Roadster with rocket thrusters, mid-air manoeuvres and a dramatic landing demonstration.

Tesla's long-delayed next-generation Roadster has taken centre stage after a demonstration featuring mid-air manoeuvres, rocket-style thrusters and a landing on its wheels, raising questions about whether flying cars could become a reality. Unveiled by Elon Musk's electric vehicle company at an event in Texas on October 15, the redesigned sports car was developed in collaboration with SpaceX, Musk's rocket company. Tesla says production is expected to begin in 2028, nearly a decade after the vehicle was first revealed. The demonstration showed the two-seater Roadster driving upside down along a ramp with the help of a suction system before lifting off, rotating in mid-air and landing. It also performed a manoeuvre in which it jumped over other Tesla vehicles. However, the demonstration does not establish that the Roadster can fly like an aircraft or function as a conventional flying car. Despite the dramatic display, several practical questions remain unanswered, including the vehicle's maximum flight altitude, the distance it can cover in the air, the final production specifications and its confirmed selling price.

How high did Tesla Roadster fly, and how far did it travel?

Tesla has not publicly confirmed the maximum altitude or horizontal distance covered by the Roadster during the demonstration. The footage showed the vehicle briefly lifting off the ground, rotating in mid-air and returning to the surface, as well as using its thrusters to jump over other vehicles. The demonstration established that the prototype could perform short airborne manoeuvres, but it did not establish the car's ability to sustain flight over long distances. The distinction is important because a vehicle that briefly leaves the ground is not necessarily capable of functioning as a flying car for everyday transportation. Sustained flight would require further information about its lift, stability, flight duration, energy consumption, control systems and safety performance. Tesla has not published independently verified figures for these capabilities. Sharing footage of the demonstration, Tesla wrote, "Real life, baby". Musk also said: "Turns out the future does have flying cars."

How does Tesla's flying Roadster work?

The Roadster combines electric vehicle technology with a system developed in collaboration with SpaceX. Its demonstration featured two main technologies: a suction system that allows the car to travel upside down along a specially designed ramp, and cold-gas thrusters that help it lift off, rotate and stabilise itself during brief airborne manoeuvres. Tesla has described the suction mechanism as a multi-mode fan and ground-sealing system that draws air from beneath the vehicle, generating downforce. This is intended to keep the car pressed against a surface even when it is upside down. Active aerodynamics and adjustable suspension are also part of the vehicle's performance-focused design. The cold-gas thrusters use pressurised gas to generate thrust, with actuators controlling their operation. Unlike a conventional car, which relies on tyre grip for acceleration and cornering, the thruster-equipped version is designed to generate additional force for specialised manoeuvres. Tesla said on X: "Every car on the road today is limited by one thing: tire grip Roadster's thruster system generates 4–5x the force the tires can. More force on the same mass means significantly better acceleration – physics does the rest,"Tesla added: "Roadster is a true pilot's car: active aerodynamics, a multi-mode suction system & cold-gas thrusters."These are company claims and have not been independently verified through publicly available performance testing. The demonstration also does not establish how the system would perform under normal road conditions or in adverse weather.

What is the Tesla Roadster's top speed and acceleration?

The Roadster's headline performance claim is acceleration from zero to 60 miles per hour (around 97 kmph) in less than one second. Tesla also says the car can exceed 230 mph (around 370 kmph). These figures were presented at the unveiling and should be treated as manufacturer claims rather than independently verified production-car performance. The acceleration target would place the Roadster among the most extreme performance vehicles if achieved in a production model. However, its claimed airborne capabilities are separate from its road performance. Tesla has not provided independently verified figures establishing how much the thruster system improves acceleration, how frequently it can be activated or how it affects the vehicle's range. The company has also not established that every version of the Roadster will offer the same capabilities.

What is the price of Tesla's flying Roadster?

Tesla has not announced a confirmed final purchase price for the redesigned Roadster. When the second-generation model was first unveiled in 2017, the company quoted a starting price of $200,000, but that figure has not been confirmed as the price of the latest version. Tesla's reservation page following the unveiling listed different deposits for different versions:

Performance: A $50,000 reservation deposit.

Thrust: A $250,000 reservation deposit for the version featuring acceleration thrusters.

Rocket: An invitation-only variant described as having a full flight system.

These amounts are reservation deposits, not confirmed final selling prices. The Rocket version is described as a single-seat vehicle, while the other configurations have different specifications. The full-flight variant is not approved for public-road use, according to reporting by The Information. The final cost could vary depending on the version, equipment and production specifications. Prospective buyers should therefore not interpret the original $200,000 estimate or the reservation deposits as confirmed prices for the redesigned car.

When will Tesla Roadster production begin?

Tesla has set 2028 as its target for beginning production of the redesigned Roadster. The timeline follows years of delays after the company first unveiled the next-generation model in 2017 and initially promised deliveries in 2020.The original Roadster, produced from 2008 to 2012, was Tesla's first electric vehicle and was built using a Lotus Elise chassis. The new model is intended to serve as a high-performance flagship, showcasing the company's engineering capabilities as Tesla expands its focus towards autonomous driving, artificial intelligence and robotics.

Can Tesla's flying Roadster be used on public roads?

The Roadster's demonstration does not mean that its airborne functions are ready for unrestricted public use. Tesla's different configurations have different stated capabilities, and the full-flight Rocket version is described as not approved for public-road use. Regulatory approval, safety standards and the practical requirements of operating a vehicle capable of leaving the ground remain key questions. A car that uses thrusters to lift off or rotate in mid-air would need to demonstrate that these operations can be carried out safely and predictably, particularly around pedestrians, other vehicles and buildings. There are also questions about how the system would affect occupants, how the vehicle would respond to a mechanical or propulsion failure, and where airborne manoeuvres could legally be performed. Tesla has yet to provide sufficient public information to establish that the Roadster can be used as a conventional flying car. For now, the unveiling demonstrates a prototype capable of brief airborne manoeuvres, not a vehicle proven to replace aircraft or routinely fly between destinations. Its maximum flight height, distance, endurance and final price remain unconfirmed.

title: Martin Phipps and Paramour agree to vacate San Antonio’s River Walk building after a $1.2 million fraud verdict and years of legal battles
summary: Representative Image of a courtroom scene depicting a legal dispute over a San Antonio property sale between longtime friends (AI-generated image)
body:
Representative Image of a courtroom scene depicting a legal dispute over a San Antonio property sale between longtime friends (AI-generated image)

A property sale between longtime friends in San Antonio has developed into a protracted legal dispute, with attorney Martin Phipps and his rooftop cocktail bar, Paramour, agreeing to surrender their spaces in a River Walk building. In late 2022, Phipps’ company, Emet LLC, agreed to sell the property at 102 Ninth St. to CDC Enterprises LP for $11 million. The deal later unravelled over a disputed $2.75 million arrangement involving the purchase price and prepaid rent, alongside allegations of unpaid rent. In late October 2025, a jury found that Phipps and his companies had committed fraud against CDC and awarded the company more than $1.2 million in damages and attorneys’ fees. The dispute continued through eviction proceedings and repeated lockouts. On October 9, 2026, the parties signed agreements requiring Phipps’ law firm and Paramour to surrender their spaces, with a limited period to remove their belongings. The agreements resolve the immediate eviction proceedings but do not establish that every financial or contractual dispute arising from the sale has been settled.

How the $11 million San Antonio property sale became a legal dispute

In late 2022, Phipps’ company, Emet LLC, agreed to sell the building at 102 Ninth St.

to CDC Enterprises, a company associated with Daren Connel, a longtime friend of Phipps. The purchase price was $11 million. According to the San Antonio Express-News, CDC financed $8.25 million of the $11 million transaction, while the remaining $2.75 million was treated as a debt in place of a cash down payment. Phipps maintained that the amount was to be credited as prepaid rent for his law firm and Paramour. CDC disputed that interpretation. Phipps maintained that the parties had agreed to treat the $2.75 million as prepaid rent credit for his law firm and Paramour. CDC disputed that interpretation, and the disagreement became central to the litigation. The building, constructed by Phipps in 2014, houses his law firm and Paramour, a rooftop cocktail bar operated by Holy Spirits LLC. The building, commonly known as the Phipps Building, has since been referred to as Paradigm, the name shown on a leasing sign described in later reporting. CDC’s ownership was upheld in the trial court, while Emet retained a contractual right to buy back the building until late 2027, subject to the terms of the agreement. The dispute illustrates how a property sale can become complicated when financing arrangements, rent credits and commercial leases are linked. The parties’ disagreement over the $2.75 million arrangement became part of a wider conflict involving ownership, unpaid rent and possession of the premises.

Paramour eviction dispute: unpaid rent claims and repeated lockouts

The disagreement extended beyond the sale contract into disputes over rent and possession of the building. In January 2024, CDC sued Holy Spirits LLC, which operates Paramour, seeking about $260,000 in alleged unpaid rent, fees and interest. CDC claimed the bar had failed to pay rent for several months. Phipps disputed the landlord’s position and argued that CDC owed money in connection with the property. These were competing claims made during the dispute, rather than findings that either party had established every allegation. In February 2024, a justice of the peace ruled in CDC’s favour in an eviction case against Holy Spirits. The company appealed the ruling later that month, moving the dispute into county court, according to the San Antonio Express-News. The conflict also led to repeated lockouts. In 2024, Phipps accused CDC of unlawfully locking out his law firm and Paramour. The dispute resurfaced in March 2026, when CDC again locked out the tenants, citing alleged unpaid rent and common-area maintenance charges. On March 18, 2026, a judge ruled that the March 2 lockout was unlawful because CDC had changed the locks without providing the required 14-day notice. The ruling did not prevent CDC from pursuing eviction through the legal process. In September 2026, CDC locked out Paramour and Phipps’ law firm for the third time since June 2024, according to the San Antonio Express-News. The landlord cited alleged unpaid rent. The lockout led to further eviction proceedings, with cases scheduled for trial on October 9. The parties signed agreements that day requiring the tenants to surrender their spaces, according to the San Antonio Express-News.

The $1.2 million jury verdict and the ruling on ownership

A major turning point came in late October 2025, when a jury ruled against Phipps and his companies in the dispute over the building. According to the San Antonio Express-News, the jury found against Phipps and his companies on CDC’s fraud claims and awarded CDC more than $1.2 million in damages and attorneys’ fees. The jury awarded Phipps’ companies nothing on their own claims. Phipps, Emet LLC, Holy Spirits LLC, his law firm and his property management firm had countersued CDC on 16 claims, including a claim seeking to have the sale contract declared void and unenforceable because of alleged fraud. During the trial, Phipps’ lawyer asked jurors to award his clients more than $5 million for lost rental income, prepaid rent and building expenses. The jury did not award them damages. Before the jury returned its verdict, State District Judge Angelica Jimenez ruled in CDC’s favour on the ownership issue, according to the San Antonio Express-News. The ruling established that CDC’s title to the property was superior to any claim by Emet LLC. Bexar County property records identify CDC as the owner. Emet LLC retains a contractual option to buy back the building until late 2027, subject to the agreement’s terms, according to the San Antonio Express-News. The jury verdict did not immediately end the wider dispute. Proceedings over rent and possession continued, with the parties returning to court over the tenants’ right to remain in the building.

Martin Phipps and Paramour agree to surrender their spaces

The latest development came on October 9, 2026, when agreements were signed resolving the pending eviction cases. The agreements require Phipps’ law firm and Paramour to surrender possession of their spaces. The agreements allow them until October 30 to remove their belongings, according to the October 12 San Antonio Express-News report. The agreements were signed on the day the eviction cases were scheduled to go to trial. They resolve those eviction proceedings, but should not be treated as proof that every financial or contractual dispute arising from the building sale has been settled. Paramour has operated at the address since 2015 and is known for its rooftop setting, cocktails and drag brunches. In late July 2026, the bar announced that it was “considering pausing this version of Paramour while we plan the next evolution,” adding that it might be forced to move. The statement did not confirm a relocation or provide a reopening date. The announcement came amid the ongoing dispute with the building’s landlord. In September, CDC locked out Paramour and Phipps’ law firm for the third time since June 2024, according to the San Antonio Express-News.

title: Durga Puja is a time for nostalgia, new clothes and hunting for bhog from pandal to pandal

body:
Let's go bhog hunting

Now, for non-Bengalis, we have to start with what the word ‘bhog’ means. Bhog is the traditional food offering made to Goddess Durga during Durga Puja, prepared with devotion and offered to the goddess before being distributed among devotees as prasad.A typical Bengali bhog plate is simple, comforting and deeply evocative: steaming khichuri made with rice and lentils, fragrant with ghee and spices, accompanied by labra, a soft, gently spiced medley of seasonal vegetables, and beguni, slices of aubergine dipped in gram-flour batter and fried until golden. There may also be tomato chutney, fried vegetables, payesh (rice pudding) and sweets, depending on the puja and local tradition. The khichuri is the heart of the meal, its soft, almost porridge-like texture carrying the warmth of lentils, rice and spices. The labra brings together the sweetness of pumpkin, the earthiness of greens and the flavour of other vegetables cooked until tender, while the beguni adds a crisp, savoury contrast. A spoonful of sweet-and-tangy chutney cuts through the richness, and payesh provides a milky, fragrant finish.

But bhog is about more than taste. Prepared in large quantities and served to hundreds of people, often by volunteers, it transforms a familiar home-style meal into a communal experience. The food is not elaborate or extravagant; its appeal lies in its freshness, generosity and the ritual of sharing. Eaten seated alongside strangers at a pandal, a plate of bhog carries the warmth of a festive kitchen and the feeling of participating in something larger than oneself. The most common memories of childhood Durga Puja—or adulthood—is to find out which pandal is serving bhog at what time, negotiate the crowd and make sure you arrive in time. If the first stop leaves you wanting more, there is always another pandal to try. The ambition is not merely to eat here. Like true Bengalis, the idea is to try bhog from as many pandals as possible, till you cannot get up from the chair, forget walking back home. For the committed bhog hunter, this is a four-day ritual. Shasti, Shaptami, Ashtami and Navami. It is a culinary expedition in which the goddess's devotees, the curious visitor and the hungry pandal hopper can find themselves united by the prospect of a good meal. Across cities, preparations have been under way for days, and the next few mornings will see thousands of people make their way to pandals for anjali and, afterwards, the much-anticipated bhog. Not every pandal serves precisely the same combination of bhog. Some offer different vegetable preparations, additional fritters or sweets, while family pujas may follow their own long-established menus. That is the part of the appeal. There is no single definitive bhog plate. So the curious has to keep exploring. And widening the girth happily.

The queue is part of the experience

A bhog hunt requires a little planning. Unlike street food stalls that operate through much of the day, bhog distribution follows the schedule of the puja and the arrangements made by individual organising committees. The food is generally served after the relevant rituals, often around midday, although timings and arrangements differ from one pandal to another. The sensible bhog hunter therefore begins with a question: where is bhog being served today, and at what time? A quick check with the organisers can prevent a wasted journey, particularly at a popular pandal where distribution may happen in batches or where coupons are required. There is also a case for looking beyond the most famous pujas. The celebrated pandals attract visitors for their scale, artistry and elaborate themes, but smaller neighbourhood pujas can offer an equally rewarding glimpse of the festival's community spirit. In many places, it is local residents and volunteers who help prepare, organise and serve the meal, turning a large logistical exercise into an expression of collective participation. The queues, in fact, are part of the experience. People arrive with children, elderly relatives and friends, waiting patiently for their turn. Volunteers move along the rows, serving portions of food and returning to refill plates. There is a certain pleasure in watching the operation come together, particularly when hundreds of people have to be fed in a relatively short period.

Bhog typically consists of Khichuri, labda, brinjal fritters, chutney and payesh

The kitchen is another story in itself. Cooking for a community means working with large quantities of rice, lentils and vegetables, coordinating the preparation of different dishes and ensuring that the food is ready at the right time. The familiar home-cooked meal becomes an exercise in organisation, requiring the efforts of cooks, organisers and volunteers who may have been working since early morning. For visitors who have grown up with bhog, the scene can bring back memories of childhood Pujo outings. For those experiencing it for the first time, it offers an accessible way to understand a festival that can otherwise appear overwhelming in its crowds, rituals and elaborate visual spectacle. And then there is the food itself. The first spoonful of steaming khichuri, the soft vegetables, the sharp sweetness of chutney and the crispness of a freshly fried beguni make a satisfying combination. It is not a meal designed to impress through novelty. Its pleasure lies in familiarity, generosity and the sense that there is enough to go around.

Why bhog tastes different

The question worth asking on a bhog trail is why this simple meal feels so special. Is it the cooking, the ritual or the company? The answer probably lies in a combination of all three. Pujo food is rarely just about taste. Meals become memorable because of the people we associate with them, the occasions on which we eat them and the rituals that surround them. A particular dish can bring back a childhood home, a family gathering or a festival that seems to return in much the same way every year. Bhog carries this emotional weight, while also introducing visitors to the idea of food as a shared offering rather than an individual indulgence. There is also something distinctive about eating alongside strangers. In a city where daily life is often organised around private schedules and separate households, a community meal briefly creates a common space. People who may never otherwise meet sit together and eat the same food, served by volunteers who are feeding an entire neighbourhood rather than a table of invited guests. That spirit of sharing is central to the experience. Bhog is offered to the goddess and then distributed among those who come to receive it. The meal's significance lies as much in this movement from offering to community as it does in the ingredients on the plate. For the bhog hunter, however, the culinary comparisons are unavoidable. One pandal's khichuri may be richer, another's labra may have a more pronounced mix of vegetables, and a particularly good beguni may become the highlight of the afternoon. These are the kinds of judgements that keep the conversation going long after the plates have been cleared. The trick is not to turn the exercise into a competition in which every pandal must be ranked. Each puja has its own traditions, resources and way of feeding people. The more interesting discovery may be how differently communities approach a meal that is familiar to almost everyone.Of course, bhog is only one part of the larger Pujo food trail. Once the afternoon's rituals and meals are over, Kolkata's streets offer another kind of feast, from phuchka and kathi rolls to chops, biryani and sweets. But these are foods to seek out between pandals, while bhog belongs to a particular time and place. One can be bought whenever a stall is open; the other asks you to arrive when the community is ready to serve. That is why the hunt is so satisfying. It gives pandal hopping a purpose beyond covering as many locations as possible. Instead of rushing from one spectacular installation to the next, the visitor has a reason to pause, wait, talk to people and take part in a tradition that is as much about community as it is about devotion.By the end of the day, the perfect bhog may still prove elusive. There will always be another pandal whose khichuri someone swears is better, another neighbourhood with a particularly memorable labra, or another plate of payesh worth returning for. The hunt can continue next year, with fresh recommendations and the same old arguments. For now, all that is required is an appetite, a little patience and a willingness to follow the aroma of freshly cooked khichuri.

body:
This festive season, take some time out for peace and mindfulness by incorporating Amethyst, Rose Quartz and Clear Quartz, three commonly used meditation crystals. Traditionally associated with self-love, mental clarity and tranquility, these stones can add meaning to your meditation practice and encourage moments of contemplation. Whether you want to unwind during the festive celebrations, raise your consciousness or develop self-compassion, each crystal provides a symbolic center point for your intention They work for beginners and meditators alike, and can help you build a ritual that encourages you to stop, breathe and reconnect to the present moment.

Key highlights

What is the purpose of Amethyst in meditation?

What are the benefits of using clear quartz during meditation?

How do you Uue rose quartz for meditation?

How do amethyst, clear quartz and rose quartz compare for meditation?

How do you choose the right crystal for meditation?

What are the best ways to use crystals during meditation?

Amethyst

Amethyst is the purple variety of quartz and is said to increase psychic awareness, intuition and tranquility. Good for those who want to meditate calmly The meditation chair features a clean silhouette and timeless style.

Benefits of amethyst meditation:

It is a stone that stabilizes and harmonizes the energy centers of the body, balancing the brain, body and spirit.

Amethyst is thought to promote the development of spiritual awareness and awakening.

Amethyst is thought to encourage clear thinking, and to improve memory, concentration and focus.

Amethyst is a gemstone that is said to aid in relieving stress, anxiety and tension.

Amethyst is thought to boost intuition by opening the third eye chakra. It can also boost your spirituality and your intuition.

Amethyst is a great addition to any relaxation or meditation practice. It lends a calm, peaceful feel.

Healing Amethyst is thought to have healing properties to help heal the physical body and feelings. Amethyst can be used to help encourage optimism and hope and to help foster a more optimistic outlook on life. It stimulates the development of new concepts and innovative thinking. It helps you to control your emotions and how to handle difficult situations.

Amethyst is a spiritual tool that can be used to promote spiritual growth, balance and relaxation. It is a great stone for boosting intuition, relieving stress or maintaining focus while meditating. Amethyst has long been associated with tranquility, meditation and spirituality. How to use amethyst gemstone:Focus on your breath or meditation cushion with the stone in your hand or in your line of sight.

Clear quartz

The most powerful healing stone is Clear Quartz. It is an opaque to translucent mineral. At the end of the day, the main things are clarity, intention and focus. Quartz clearing is a technique that may aid people who are having difficulty focusing during meditation to refocus. In this technique the person is anchored in the present.

Here are the benefits of clear quartz for meditation:

Encourages setting intentions Use as a physical reminder of your meditation intention.

This clean look may be used as the primary object of visual meditation, promoting mindful attention .

Represents mental clarity: A lot of crystal lovers connect it with balanced intellect and consciousness.

How to use it: Before starting your breathing exercise, place the clear quartz in front of you and observe its transparency, shape and reflections for one minute. Close your eyes.

Rose Quartz

Rose Quartz is the stone of self love, compassion, love and warmth. Fondly known as the Pink quartz. Loving-kindness meditation is a great way to cultivate positive emotions and feelings toward self and others this season.

Advantages of meditating on Rose Quartz

It can be a reminder to treat yourself more kindly. Be positive with yourself.

Compassion and connection have long been linked to loving-kindness meditation.

Paint the meditation room a soft pink to create a warm and intimate mood and a peaceful ritual. How to use it: Hold the rose quartz to your heart and silently repeat the phrases “May I be at peace” or “May I be kinder to myself.”

Clear quartzClarity and intentionFocus and concentrationVisual meditation

Rose quartzLove and compassionSelf-acceptance and kindnessLoving-kindness meditation

How to choose the right crystal for your meditation practice?

You don't have to make selecting a meditation crystal complicated. Start by thinking about the contribution you want to make to your practice.If its symbolism and appearance help to bring about a peaceful state of mind then amethyst is a good choice for a calming ritual. Use clear quartz as a visual aid to help you return to your breath when your attention drifts for better concentration.To encourage self-love and compassion, use rose quartz to complement affirmations and loving-kindness meditation. There is no one crystal that is the best for meditation. The best one is the one that works for you, and that also helps you stick with your practice.

Ways to meditate with crystals

Establish a quiet atmosphere Find a comfortable place where you won’t be interrupted. Choose your intention: Do you want to focus on compassion, awareness or calmness? You can hold it in your hands and look at it, or you can place it near you. Breathe normally and slowly and use the crystal as an anchor.If you are new to meditation, start with a short meditation session and then work your way up to five to ten minutes. Then reflect on how you felt and if the practice helped you concentrate. Remember that the research supporting the benefits of meditation is stronger than the research supporting the healing properties of crystals. Crystals are fun mindfulness tools but not a substitute for research-based medical or mental health care.

FAQ's

Which crystal is best for meditation?

Amethyst, clear quartz and rose quartz are three popular options. Amethyst is traditionally associated with calmness, clear quartz with clarity and focus, and rose quartz with compassion and self-love. The best choice depends on your personal preferences and meditation goals.

How long should I meditate with a crystal?

Start with five to ten minutes per session. Focus on your breathing and use the crystal as a reminder to return your attention to the present whenever your mind wanders.

Can I use all three crystals together?

Yes. You can place amethyst, clear quartz and rose quartz together in your meditation space. You might also select one crystal per session based on the intention you want to explore.

Should I hold a crystal or place it nearby while meditating?

Both options are suitable. Holding a crystal provides a tactile point of focus, while placing it nearby allows you to use it as a visual anchor. Choose whichever feels most comfortable.

Do I need to cleanse my crystals before meditation?

Crystal traditions often recommend cleansing crystals as part of a ritual. However, there is no scientific evidence that energetic cleansing is necessary. If you choose to clean a physical crystal, use a method appropriate for its mineral properties and avoid water or salt when the material may be damaged.

summary: A child struggles to put on their shoes, and the parent resists the urge to do it for them.
body:
Photo: Canva

A child struggles to put on their shoes, and the parent resists the urge to do it for them. At a restaurant, a child is encouraged to place their own order instead of letting an adult speak on their behalf. And when a child finds a playground challenge difficult, the parent offers support without immediately stepping in to solve the problem. These everyday moments reflect an approach to parenting that gives children more opportunities to try things for themselves, make decisions and learn from mistakes. Parenting coach Hitesh Mathur recently highlighted three Danish-inspired habits for raising confident children in a video shared on his Instagram account, @parentingwithbrainify. According to Mathur, confidence does not grow simply from hearing adults say, “You're amazing.” It also develops when children face manageable challenges and discover that they can handle them. This idea is linked to a psychological concept called self-efficacy, a person's belief in their ability to do something or deal with a particular situation. It is not a guarantee that a child will always succeed. It is the belief that they can make an attempt, learn and try again.

Give children real responsibilities instead of doing everything for them

Mathur suggests giving children age-appropriate responsibilities, such as ordering their own food, preparing a simple snack, making small decisions or speaking to someone when appropriate. The point is not to leave children to manage everything alone. It is to let them take part in everyday tasks instead of assuming they cannot handle them. For example, a parent visiting a restaurant with a young child could help them understand the menu and then let them tell the server what they would like. At home, a child could choose between two suitable outfits, pack their school bag with a checklist or help prepare breakfast. These tasks may seem ordinary, but they give children a chance to practise making decisions and handling the results. When they complete something they initially found difficult, they have a concrete reason to believe they can do it again.A 2006 study published in Contemporary Educational Psychology examined the sources of self-efficacy beliefs among 263 students entering middle school. Researchers found that mastery experiences were the strongest predictor of students' academic and self-regulatory self-efficacy among the factors examined. The study focused on school-related beliefs, not everyday parenting tasks. Still, its findings support the broader idea that confidence in one's abilities can grow through experience, rather than encouragement alone.

Allow manageable risks instead of stopping every attempt

Another habit Mathur recommends is allowing children to explore, climb, try unfamiliar activities and take manageable risks without an adult immediately telling them to stop. For parents, this can be difficult. It is natural to want to prevent a fall, a spill or a moment of frustration. But stepping in at the first sign of difficulty can also mean that children miss opportunities to learn what they can handle. A child learning to ride a bicycle, for instance, may need time to wobble, lose balance and try again. A child climbing playground equipment may need to assess where to place their feet and decide whether they can reach the next step. This does not mean allowing children to face dangers they cannot reasonably understand or manage. Parents should consider the child's age, ability and surroundings, stay appropriately involved and intervene when there is a genuine safety concern. Parents must distinguish between a situation that is dangerous and one that is simply unfamiliar or challenging. A 2023 study analysed data from 9,221 adolescents in Norway. It found that adolescents who reported experiences of mastering tasks had higher self-efficacy scores. Support from parents, friends and teachers was also associated with higher scores.

Do not rush to rescue them when something gets difficult

Mathur's third suggestion is to resist immediately solving a problem when a child is struggling. Parents can stay close, offer reassurance and help when needed, while allowing the child some time to work out what to do. Imagine a child building a tower that keeps falling. An adult could rebuild it for them, explain exactly what to do or simply take over. Another option is to ask, "What do you think would make it stronger?" and let the child experiment. The same approach can work with puzzles, homework, simple household tasks and disagreements with friends, provided the child is not left distressed or dealing with a problem beyond their ability. There is an important difference between support and taking over. Support helps a child approach a challenge; taking over can unintentionally send the message that the adult does not believe the child can manage it. Parents do not have to remain silent or refuse help. They can offer a hint, demonstrate one step or break a task into smaller parts. If the child is overwhelmed, stepping in more directly may be the right response.

Why confidence involves more than telling children they are amazing

Praise can make children feel appreciated, but praise alone does not give them experience in handling a difficult task. A child may hear that they are brilliant and still feel unsure when they encounter something they have never tried before. Self-efficacy develops in specific situations. A child may feel confident about swimming but uncertain about speaking in class. Experience with one task does not automatically remove every other fear. Parents can help by recognising effort and progress while being specific about what the child did. Instead of only saying, "You're amazing," they might say, "You kept trying different ways until you worked out how to do it." This gives children something concrete to remember the next time a task feels difficult.

title: 99-year-old Helga Duffy strapped herself to a plane’s wing and flew through the skies to break the record for the oldest female wing-walker, while raising £1,300 for an air ambulance
summary: At an age when many people prefer to keep their feet firmly on the ground, Helga Duffy strapped herself to the wing of a plane and took to the skies.
body:
Image: Jam Press/ Guinness World Records

At an age when many people prefer to keep their feet firmly on the ground, Helga Duffy strapped herself to the wing of a plane and took to the skies. The 99-year-old set a Guinness World Records title for the oldest female wing-walker after completing the daring flight at RFC Rendcomb Airfield in Cirencester, Gloucestershire, on October 16, 2026. Inspired by another woman who performed the same stunt at 97, Duffy decided to pursue the extraordinary challenge herself. But her achievement was about more than breaking a record. The German-born woman also raised more than £1,300 for Wiltshire and Bath Air Ambulance, turning her adventurous flight into a fundraising effort for a service with a deeply personal connection to her family.

97-year-old inspired Helga Duffy to break a wing-walking record

Duffy's decision to attempt the record was inspired by Elizabeth “Betty” Bromage, who had made headlines after performing a wing walk at the age of 97. Bromage had regained the Guinness World Records title for the oldest female wing-walker following a flight on August 4, 2026, when she was 97 years and 145 days old. After seeing coverage of Bromage's achievement, Duffy decided she wanted to try the stunt herself. Her attempt was originally planned for September 23, her 99th birthday, but was postponed until October 16.A Guinness World Records adjudicator attended the flight at RFC Rendcomb Airfield to verify the achievement and present Duffy with an official certificate.

She was 99 years and 21 days old when she completed the attempt, establishing a new record in the female category. Bromage congratulated Duffy but suggested the competition might not be over. The BBC reported that she hoped to attempt the feat again when she turned 100, potentially reclaiming the title. Her response added another chapter to the unusual story of two women pushing the boundaries of what is possible at an advanced age.

‘I wasn't frightened because I was so excited’

Duffy described the experience of being strapped to the top of a small aircraft as “peculiar”, but said excitement had kept fear at bay.“I wasn't frightened because I was so excited,” she said, according to the BBC.Wing-walking involves being securely harnessed to the outside of an aircraft, usually on its upper wing, while the plane is in flight. The activity requires specialist equipment, an experienced pilot and careful preparation. For Duffy, however, the challenge was also a chance to demonstrate that reaching an advanced age did not mean she had lost her appetite for trying something different. Her nieces, Jackie Rose and Julie Preece, watched the flight. They described her as an independent and forthright woman who had wanted to do something different for a long time. Rose said Duffy wanted to show that, despite being 99, she was still the person she had always been. The achievement was therefore about more than the record itself. It reflected her determination to pursue a personal ambition rather than let her age define what she could attempt.

Raising more than £1,300 for an air ambulance

Alongside the record attempt, Duffy raised more than £1,300 for Wiltshire and Bath Air Ambulance, a charity that provides emergency medical care to people across the region. The fundraising carried particular meaning for her family. Rose and Preece told the BBC that their mother had made her final journey in an air ambulance, giving them a personal connection to the service Duffy chose to support. The charitable purpose gave the flight an additional dimension. Duffy was not simply attempting to establish an unusual record. She was using the attention surrounding her achievement to support a service that can be critical when patients need urgent medical assistance. The reported fundraising total of more than £1,300 added a practical outcome to the challenge, allowing Duffy to turn a personal milestone into support for an organisation serving people in medical emergencies.

A family memory behind the achievement

Duffy's achievement also prompted reflection on her late father. She was the eldest of seven children and said she believed he would have been proud of her accomplishment.“He expected the best of us. So I always tried,” she said, adding that she hoped her father would be proud of his firstborn if he were still somewhere watching over her. The remark offered a glimpse into the personal significance of the milestone. While the world-record certificate recognised the flight itself, Duffy's comments suggested that the achievement also connected her present-day adventure with the expectations and memories of her childhood. Duffy lives in a care home in Devizes, Wiltshire, and previously lived in Frome, Somerset, for many years. Her nieces' support during the record attempt reflected the family encouragement surrounding the challenge.

The record may not stand unchallenged

Duffy's achievement has put her name in the record books, but Bromage has suggested that she may try to take the title back when she turns 100.Bromage had completed several wing walks by the time of the BBC report and had also used her stunts to raise money for charitable causes. Her determination to return to the skies means Duffy's record could face another challenge if Bromage follows through on her plans.At 99 years and 21 days old, Helga Duffy has set a Guinness World Records title as the oldest female wing-walker, proving that age has not stopped her from taking on extraordinary challenges. Her achievement combines an extraordinary physical feat with personal determination and charitable fundraising. Inspired by another woman who showed what was possible at 97, Duffy took her own turn in the skies at 99, supporting an air ambulance service along the way. If Bromage attempts to reclaim the title at 100, the record could become the next chapter in an unusual rivalry between two women determined to keep flying.

title: Psychology says children can find it harder to concentrate when a sibling is doing something more interesting
entities: What Children Learn Without Being Taught
summary: A child is halfway through a maths worksheet when their older sibling starts building a Lego tower nearby.
body:
sibling’s play can make it harder for a child to focus on homework.

A child is halfway through a maths worksheet when their older sibling starts building a Lego tower nearby. Within minutes, the pencil is down, the chair has been abandoned, and the child is asking to join in. At another time, the same child may sit quietly through a story or finish a puzzle without much difficulty. So why does concentration suddenly become harder when a sibling has something more exciting to do? For many Indian families, this is a familiar scene. Children may share a bedroom, study table or living space, making it difficult for one child to focus while another watches cartoons, plays a game or builds something nearby. Even when nobody is deliberately disturbing them, the more interesting activity can be difficult to ignore.

28 Sept 2026 | 08:18

Does your teenager tell you about their friends, or do you often have to ask? How much do you know about their social life?

Psychology offers a useful explanation: concentration is not just about trying hard. It also involves filtering out distractions, controlling impulses and staying with a task that may be less immediately rewarding. These abilities develop throughout childhood, and an exciting activity nearby can make them harder to use.

What Children Learn Without Being Taught

Children are still developing the ability to resist distractions.

Why a sibling's play can be difficult to ignore

Imagine a six-year-old trying to finish a Hindi writing exercise while their younger sibling laughs at a cartoon. The child may know what they are supposed to do, but their attention keeps drifting towards the sounds and movement around them. This involves selective attention - the ability to focus on relevant information while filtering out competing distractions.A 2022 study published in Developmental Science, titled “Attentional control in middle childhood is highly dynamic”, examined children aged four to 10 years and adults performing a visual task while unexpected sounds played in the background. The researchers found that novel sounds distracted children, with younger children particularly affected. Children aged four and five remained distracted throughout the experiment, while older children increasingly adapted to the sounds as the task progressed. The experiment did not specifically involve siblings, but it helps explain why children may struggle to ignore an interesting sound or activity while concentrating on something else.In everyday family life, a sibling's game, a funny video or an animated conversation can be more compelling than copying spellings or completing a worksheet. The contrast becomes especially noticeable when the child's own task requires sustained effort.

The more interesting activity may feel more rewarding

Another factor is the difference between what a child has to do and what they want to do. Homework, handwriting practice and revision often involve delayed rewards. A child has to finish several questions before getting a break. A sibling's activity, on the other hand, offers immediate enjoyment, novelty or social interaction. This does not necessarily mean the child is deliberately disobedient. They may simply be finding it difficult to resist an appealing alternative. Executive functions - the mental skills involved in controlling impulses, holding information in mind and switching between tasks - develop throughout childhood. These abilities help children stay with a task even when something more attractive is happening nearby. Sibling interactions can also provide opportunities to practise these skills. Playing together may require children to wait for a turn, negotiate rules, plan and manage frustration. However, enjoying an activity with a sibling and concentrating independently while that sibling plays are two different situations. The same relationship can offer opportunities for learning while also creating moments when attention becomes harder to maintain.

Breaking homework into smaller tasks may help children stay focused.

Why “just concentrate” may not work

When a child repeatedly looks away from their books to watch a sibling play, parents may interpret it as laziness, a lack of discipline or an attempt to avoid studying. But repeatedly telling a child to concentrate does not remove the distraction competing for their attention. Research on background television offers a useful parallel. In a 2008 experiment published in Child Development, researchers observed children aged 12, 24 and 36 months playing with toys, with and without a television programme playing in the background. Although the children looked at the television only briefly, its presence significantly reduced the length of their play episodes and their focused attention.A sibling is not the same as a television. They can speak directly to the child, invite them to play and introduce new ideas. Their activity can also carry emotional significance: the child may be curious, excited or worried about missing out. Still, the study illustrates an important point: a distraction does not have to hold a child's attention continuously to interrupt what they are doing. Rather than assuming a child is unwilling to work, parents can first examine whether the environment is making concentration unnecessarily difficult.

Does having a sibling make children less focused?

Not necessarily. Growing up with siblings can also offer opportunities to develop important thinking and social skills.A 2023 longitudinal study published in Psychology in Russia: State of the Art followed 490 children who were initially five to six years old. It found that children who watched videos or played video games with siblings showed greater gains in certain measures of inhibitory control over a year than children who generally did these activities alone. Inhibitory control is the ability to resist an automatic response and do what a situation requires. It is relevant when a child wants to leave their homework to join a sibling but needs to finish the current task first. However, the study examined shared digital activities, not distraction during homework. Its findings do not establish that playing with siblings directly improves concentration during schoolwork. They do suggest that sibling interactions can be associated with the development of skills children use to manage their behaviour. The takeaway is not that siblings are bad for concentration. Rather, children need opportunities both to interact with their siblings and to practise focusing independently.

What parents can do when one child keeps getting distracted

For families living in Indian cities, separating siblings into different rooms may not always be practical. A shared bedroom, a compact flat or a single dining table used for homework can make it difficult to create completely separate spaces. Small changes, however, can make the task more manageable.1. Create a quieter window for homeworkIf one child needs to study while another is playing, try scheduling a short period when the more exciting activity is paused or moved elsewhere. This does not mean keeping siblings silent throughout the evening. Even a brief, predictable period with fewer distractions may help.2. Break work into smaller sectionsInstead of saying, “Finish all your maths before you get up,” try setting a manageable goal: complete five sums, check the answers and then take a short break. Smaller goals can make it easier for a child to see progress and return to the task after resting.3. Avoid comparing siblingsStatements such as “Look at your sister, she has already finished” can make homework more emotionally charged. The child may begin to associate studying with comparison rather than learning. Focus instead on individual progress: “You finished these five questions. Let's see what you can do next.”4. Explain when it is time to work and when it is time to playChildren can learn simple, consistent rules. Parents might say, “Your brother can keep building his tower, but this is your ten-minute writing time. When the timer rings, you can take a break.”The aim is not to make the child feel guilty for wanting to play. It is to help them understand that different activities have different times.5. Make room for shared playIt is equally important not to treat every sibling interaction as an interruption. Playing together, negotiating rules, taking turns and resolving disagreements can offer opportunities to practise social and cognitive skills. The goal is to balance shared activities with time for individual responsibilities.

When should parents pay closer attention?

Occasionally struggling to concentrate when a sibling is doing something exciting is not, by itself, evidence of an attention problem. Age, temperament, sleep, interest in the task and the surrounding environment can all influence how easily a child focuses. Parents can observe whether the difficulty occurs mainly when there is an obvious distraction or whether it also appears in quieter settings, during conversations, play, meals and other everyday routines.If persistent attention difficulties affect schoolwork, relationships or daily life across settings, it may be worth discussing them with a paediatrician or qualified child mental health professional. Ultimately, a child who abandons a worksheet to watch their sibling build a tower may not be making a statement about their attitude towards learning. They may simply be finding it difficult to resist something more engaging in that moment. For parents, the useful question is not only, “Why won't my child concentrate?” It is also, “What is competing for their attention, and how can I make it easier for them to return to what they need to do?”Sometimes, helping a child focus begins not with another reminder to pay attention, but with a small change to the environment around them.

The child may know what they are supposed to do, but their attention keeps drifting towards the sounds and movement around them. This involves selective attention - the ability to focus on relevant information while filtering out competing distractions.A 2022 study published in Developmental Science, titled “Attentional control in middle childhood is highly dynamic”, examined children aged four to 10 years and adults performing a visual task while unexpected sounds played in the background. The researchers found that novel sounds distracted children, with younger children particularly affected. Children aged four and five remained distracted throughout the experiment, while older children increasingly adapted to the sounds as the task progressed. The experiment did not specifically involve siblings, but it helps explain why children may struggle to ignore an interesting sound or activity while concentrating on something else.In everyday family life, a sibling's game, a funny video or an animated conversation can be more compelling than copying spellings or completing a worksheet. The contrast becomes especially noticeable when the child's own task requires sustained effort.
The more interesting activity may feel more rewarding

Another factor is the difference between what a child has to do and what they want to do. Homework, handwriting practice and revision often involve delayed rewards. A child has to finish several questions before getting a break. A sibling's activity, on the other hand, offers immediate enjoyment, novelty or social interaction. This does not necessarily mean the child is deliberately disobedient. They may simply be finding it difficult to resist an appealing alternative. Executive functions - the mental skills involved in controlling impulses, holding information in mind and switching between tasks - develop throughout childhood. These abilities help children stay with a task even when something more attractive is happening nearby. Sibling interactions can also provide opportunities to practise these skills. Playing together may require children to wait for a turn, negotiate rules, plan and manage frustration. However, enjoying an activity with a sibling and concentrating independently while that sibling plays are two different situations. The same relationship can offer opportunities for learning while also creating moments when attention becomes harder to maintain.
Breaking homework into smaller tasks may help children stay focused.
Why “just concentrate” may not work

When a child repeatedly looks away from their books to watch a sibling play, parents may interpret it as laziness, a lack of discipline or an attempt to avoid studying. But repeatedly telling a child to concentrate does not remove the distraction competing for their attention. Research on background television offers a useful parallel. In a 2008 experiment published in Child Development, researchers observed children aged 12, 24 and 36 months playing with toys, with and without a television programme playing in the background. Although the children looked at the television only briefly, its presence significantly reduced the length of their play episodes and their focused attention.A sibling is not the same as a television. They can speak directly to the child, invite them to play and introduce new ideas. Their activity can also carry emotional significance: the child may be curious, excited or worried about missing out. Still, the study illustrates an important point: a distraction does not have to hold a child's attention continuously to interrupt what they are doing. Rather than assuming a child is unwilling to work, parents can first examine whether the environment is making concentration unnecessarily difficult.
Does having a sibling make children less focused?

Not necessarily. Growing up with siblings can also offer opportunities to develop important thinking and social skills.A 2023 longitudinal study published in Psychology in Russia: State of the Art followed 490 children who were initially five to six years old. It found that children who watched videos or played video games with siblings showed greater gains in certain measures of inhibitory control over a year than children who generally did these activities alone. Inhibitory control is the ability to resist an automatic response and do what a situation requires. It is relevant when a child wants to leave their homework to join a sibling but needs to finish the current task first. However, the study examined shared digital activities, not distraction during homework. Its findings do not establish that playing with siblings directly improves concentration during schoolwork. They do suggest that sibling interactions can be associated with the development of skills children use to manage their behaviour. The takeaway is not that siblings are bad for concentration. Rather, children need opportunities both to interact with their siblings and to practise focusing independently.
What parents can do when one child keeps getting distracted

For families living in Indian cities, separating siblings into different rooms may not always be practical. A shared bedroom, a compact flat or a single dining table used for homework can make it difficult to create completely separate spaces. Small changes, however, can make the task more manageable.1. Create a quieter window for homeworkIf one child needs to study while another is playing, try scheduling a short period when the more exciting activity is paused or moved elsewhere. This does not mean keeping siblings silent throughout the evening. Even a brief, predictable period with fewer distractions may help.2. Break work into smaller sectionsInstead of saying, “Finish all your maths before you get up,” try setting a manageable goal: complete five sums, check the answers and then take a short break. Smaller goals can make it easier for a child to see progress and return to the task after resting.3. Avoid comparing siblingsStatements such as “Look at your sister, she has already finished” can make homework more emotionally charged. The child may begin to associate studying with comparison rather than learning. Focus instead on individual progress: “You finished these five questions. Let's see what you can do next.”4. Explain when it is time to work and when it is time to playChildren can learn simple, consistent rules. Parents might say, “Your brother can keep building his tower, but this is your ten-minute writing time. When the timer rings, you can take a break.”The aim is not to make the child feel guilty for wanting to play. It is to help them understand that different activities have different times.5. Make room for shared playIt is equally important not to treat every sibling interaction as an interruption. Playing together, negotiating rules, taking turns and resolving disagreements can offer opportunities to practise social and cognitive skills. The goal is to balance shared activities with time for individual responsibilities.
When should parents pay closer attention?

Occasionally struggling to concentrate when a sibling is doing something exciting is not, by itself, evidence of an attention problem. Age, temperament, sleep, interest in the task and the surrounding environment can all influence how easily a child focuses. Parents can observe whether the difficulty occurs mainly when there is an obvious distraction or whether it also appears in quieter settings, during conversations, play, meals and other everyday routines.If persistent attention difficulties affect schoolwork, relationships or daily life across settings, it may be worth discussing them with a paediatrician or qualified child mental health professional. Ultimately, a child who abandons a worksheet to watch their sibling build a tower may not be making a statement about their attitude towards learning. They may simply be finding it difficult to resist something more engaging in that moment. For parents, the useful question is not only, “Why won't my child concentrate?” It is also, “What is competing for their attention, and how can I make it easier for them to return to what they need to do?”Sometimes, helping a child focus begins not with another reminder to pay attention, but with a small change to the environment around them.

title: 'Hope better sense prevails': SC flags traders' livelihood concerns as Delhi braces for CJP's Tiranga march
summary: SC declines urgent plea against Central Park closure ahead of ’s Tiranga march
body:
SC declines urgent plea against Central Park closure ahead of ’s Tiranga march

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined an urgent hearing on a plea challenging the New Delhi Municipal Council's decision to shut Central Park in Connaught Place ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed ‘Lehra do Tiranga’ protest, saying it hoped “better sense will prevail” among all concerned.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it was conscious of the difficulties that a closure could cause to small shopkeepers and their families, while observing that the right to protest, the need to maintain law and order and the livelihood of traders were interconnected issues.

‘Sit Down With PM Modi’: Mary Millben, CJP Founder Dipke Clash Over ‘US Donors Funding’ Claim “We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers earn their livelihood during these days. We know the hardship and difficulty entire families will face,” the bench said. Justice Bagchi said the court could intervene if the restrictions resulted in business losses, adding that it would consider exercising its constitutional jurisdiction if required."If there's loss of business, we will exercise our powers under Constitutional jurisdiction. Let's cross that bridge when it comes," Justice Bagchi said.

During the hearing, the petitioner's lawyer submitted that the NDMC had issued directions late Thursday night to close Central Park, effectively preventing businesses from operating in the area. The civic body had announced that the park would remain closed to the public on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons. The bench indicated that the plea could be listed on October 26 or 27.

CJP says protest will go ahead

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has called on citizens to gather at Central Park with the national flag at 5 pm on Friday, alleging that party members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were jailed for unfurling the Tricolour. The party has said it will proceed with the march despite the closure of the park and security restrictions.In a post on X, Dipke defended the party's protests, rejected allegations that it was promoting anarchy and accused the government of restricting democratic rights."Businesses do not suffer because of peaceful protests. They suffer when the govt decides to shut down an entire city, suspend internet services and restrict the movement of its own citizens and turn the city into a war-zone.""Since its inception, the Cockroach Janta Party has maintained that we will always follow Mahatma Gandhi’s path of peace and non-violence, and we have stood by that commitment. We have organised protests in Mumbai, Pune, Jaipur, Lucknow, Bengaluru and Nagpur, and every single one of them has been peaceful. I was personally assaulted in Jaipur, but even then, I chose not to retaliate because responding to violence with violence goes against everything we believe in. We would rather exercise the rights guaranteed to us by the Constitution, drafted under the leadership of Dr. BR Ambedkar, than resort to physical force. Our strength comes from our commitment to constitutional values, and no amount of provocation will make us abandon them.""Despite this, there are constant attempts to portray us as anarchists simply because we refuse to remain silent. But demanding answers from the govt is not anarchy, protesting against injustice on the streets is not anarchy, and questioning those who hold public office is certainly not anarchy. These are the most fundamental expressions of democracy. The very party that is in power today spent decades organising protests, taking to the streets and questioning the governments of the day when it was in opposition. Had the same restrictions, intimidation and police crackdowns been used against them, many of those who occupy positions of power today might never have reached where they are. It is deeply hypocritical to celebrate protests as a democratic right when you are in opposition and treat the same act as a threat to public order when you come to power."ALSO READ: ‘No one called Mahatma Gandhi African’: Sanjay Raut slams order against actor Imran Khan"We are not asking for privileges or special treatment. We are simply asking to exercise the rights that belong to every citizen of this Republic, irrespective of which party is in power. So let us fulfil our duty as citizens of this country by questioning those we elect, demanding accountability and speaking up whenever we witness injustice.""A govt that has been elected by the people is bound to listen to the people, not silence them. Democracy does not end once the votes have been counted."

Security tightened ahead of ‘Lehra do Tiranga’ march

The proposed demonstration comes amid a standoff between the CJP and Delhi Police over protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The CJP had announced the march after Das and Ranka were arrested for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site, and raising slogans demanding Kumar's resignation. They were subsequently remanded to five days of judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail. Dipke has urged political parties and civil society organisations to set aside ideological differences and join the demonstration."I request all political parties and civil society groups to rise above ideology and come together. If the right to vote is not saved, democracy will not be saved," Dipke said at a press conference on Thursday.He also questioned the scale of voter deletions during the SIR exercise and alleged that the revisions could affect electoral outcomes."The margin of victory in 2024 was just 2 per cent. Over 13 crore voters deleted -- around 14 percent," he said."Where 2 per cent is deciding the election, you are deleting 13 crore votes. What is this if not a setting?" he added. The CJP has alleged that the government is shielding Kumar from scrutiny. These allegations have not been established by the court.

Police cite law and order concerns

Delhi Police has said Connaught Place is not a designated site for protests and that demonstrations can be held at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the requisite permissions."Jantar Mantar has been denotified as a designated protest site. Protesters can hold demonstrations at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the requisite permission," a senior police officer said. Security has been tightened around Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar, with several companies of paramilitary personnel stationed in the national capital. Police are deploying personnel at strategic locations, erecting barricades and regulating the movement of protesters and commuters to prevent any untoward incident. The NDMC issued its closure notice on Thursday, stating that Central Park would remain shut on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons. The decision came a day after the CJP announced its proposed march at the park, located in the centre of Connaught Place's inner circle. The party's agitation began in Mumbai on October 2 and subsequently moved to Delhi. On October 10, a planned demonstration at Jantar Mantar was met with a police crackdown, with Dipke, Das and Ranka detained at the airport after arriving from Mumbai. Opposition leaders, activists and students were also detained during protests in the capital.

Join conversation

Share your thoughts in the comments

Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On October 13, CJP members entered the barricaded Jantar Mantar site carrying the national flag and were detained. Opposition parties and student organisations have separately held demonstrations against the SIR exercise and demanded accountability from the Election Commission. INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission headquarters on October 6 and were stopped by police barricades. Opposition leaders later met President Droupadi Murmu on October 9 to raise their concerns. The CJP has since framed its proposed Connaught Place march as a campaign for voting rights and the constitutional right to protest, setting up another confrontation over the restrictions imposed on demonstrations in central Delhi.
